text:
Rasmus Dahlin is off to a slower start than usual, as Matthew Fairburn put it in his game-day notebook, and the Sabres have gone with him: 12 points in 18 games and a run of losses in the back half of his last ten. His scoring rate is 1.62 points per 60 after 2.38 last season.

The underlying numbers are not the problem. Buffalo takes 54% of the shot attempts and 52% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, and nothing here is luck in either direction: his goals match his chances, and his team's on-ice scoring is close to what the chances deserve. The difference from last year is volume. He's creating fewer chances for himself (0.42 expected goals per 60 after 0.47), and fewer of the team's looks end in his assists.

He's still the passer he was. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him 12th of 215 defensemen. The passes are still there; they just aren't turning into points yet.
